mainTopic: Daily-routine ברכות (bathroom, bedtime, morning), and blessing God for the bad as for the good
overview: The גמרא lists the ברכות and short prayers a person says throughout an ordinary day. It begins with entering the bathroom: a prayer to the מלאכים, which אביי rewrites, and the ברכה of אשר יצר on leaving. רב, שמואל and רב ששת argue over how אשר יצר should end, and רב פפא combines two of their endings. Next come bedtime קריאת שמע with המפיל, and then the morning ברכות: אלהי נשמה, a ברכה for each step of getting up, the מצוה-ברכות for ציצית, תפילין and נטילת ידים, and המעביר שינה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rule that one blesses for the bad as for the good. רבא explains that this means accepting bad news with joy, not saying the same ברכה. Four different פסוקים are brought as sources, followed by the habit of saying 'כל דעביד רחמנא לטב עביד'. The amud ends with the story of רבי עקיבא, whose losses one night saved his life, and his closing sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: The prayer before entering the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: A person entering the בית הכסא asks the accompanying מלאכים to step away until he comes back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever enters a bathroom says: 'Be honored, honorable holy ones, servants of the One on High. Give honor to the God of Israel. Leave me until I go in, do what I need, and come back to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short prayer that a person says to the מלאכים who escort him, right before he goes into the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that holy מלאכים always accompany a person. A bathroom is not a dignified place for them. So the person respectfully asks them to wait outside until he returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Servants of the One on High (the מלאכים)
Leave me / let go of me
My will, i.e. my bodily needs

phrases.english: One who enters a bathroom says:
Be honored, honorable holy ones,
phrases.notes: Addressed to the מלאכים who accompany a person.

phrases.english: servants of the One on High,
give honor to the God of Israel,
leave me until I enter
and do my will, and come back to you.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before entering the bathroom, one asks the escorting מלאכים to leave him until he comes out.

steps.title: אביי rejects that wording and gives a better prayer
steps.stepSummary: אביי says not to ask the מלאכים to leave, because they might not come back. Instead one asks them to guard him and wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A person should not say this, because maybe the angels will leave him and go away for good. Instead he should say: 'Guard me, guard me; help me, help me; support me, support me; wait for me, wait for me, until I go in and come out, for this is the way of people.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי objects to the prayer from Step 1 and replaces it with a new version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with 'leave me' is that it could cause the מלאכים to actually abandon the person and never return. אביי's version keeps them close: it asks them to protect him and to wait just outside. It ends by explaining that this is simply a normal human need.

keyTerms.meaning: They will abandon him and go
The way of human beings (a natural need)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא לֵימָא אִינָשׁ הָכִי,
phrases.english: Abaye said: A person should not say this,
lest they abandon him and go.
Rather, he should say: Guard me, guard me,
help me, help me, support me, support me,
wait for me, wait for me
until I enter and come out,
for such is the way of human beings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא לֵימָא אִינָשׁ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wording of Step 1 and replaces it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the wording of the prayer is rejected. The practice of addressing the מלאכים before entering stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Saying 'leave me' risks the מלאכים abandoning the person permanently.

steps.title: The blessing on leaving the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: On leaving, one says the ברכה of אשר יצר, praising God for the wise design of the human body.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he comes out, he says: 'Blessed... Who formed man with wisdom and created in him many openings and many hollow spaces. It is revealed and known before Your Throne of Glory that if one of them were to open, or one of them were to become blocked, it would be impossible to stay alive and stand before You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the text of the ברכה said on leaving the bathroom, which we know as אשר יצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה thanks God for the body's openings and inner cavities working properly. If even one of them opened when it should not, or became blocked, a person could not survive. The ending of the ברכה is not given here, which sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Who formed (the opening words of the ברכה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the ברכת אשר יצר that is said every day.

phrases.english: When he goes out, he says:
Blessed... Who formed man with wisdom,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָרָא בּוֹ נְקָבִים נְקָבִים, חֲלָלִים חֲלָלִים,
phrases.english: and created in him many openings and many cavities,
it is revealed and known before Your Throne of Glory
that if one of them were to open
or if one of them were to be blocked
it would be impossible to stand before You.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On leaving the bathroom, one recites the ברכה of אשר יצר.

steps.title: How does the blessing end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the closing words (the חתימה) of אשר יצר should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does he conclude the blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The text in Step 3 had no closing line, so the גמרא asks what the ending should be. The next steps give the answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A long ברכה ends with a closing phrase that sums up its theme. The question is which phrase best sums up the theme of אשר יצר.

keyTerms.meaning: He concludes / seals (the closing of a ברכה)

phrases.english: With what does he conclude?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct closing phrase for the ברכה of אשר יצר.

steps.title: רב: end with Healer of the sick
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ברכה ends with 'רופא חולים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: 'Healer of the sick.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: end the ברכה with 'Healer of the sick'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב sees the body's healthy functioning as a kind of ongoing healing from God, so he picks a healing theme for the ending.

phrases.english: Rav said: Healer of the sick.

steps.title: שמואל objects: not everyone is sick
steps.stepSummary: שמואל argues that רב's ending makes everyone sound sick, and suggests 'רופא כל בשר' instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: אבא (רב) has made the whole world sick! Rather, end with: 'Healer of all flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל challenges רב's ending and offers his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy person saying 'Healer of the sick' would be calling himself sick. שמואל keeps the healing theme but widens it to 'all flesh'. That way it describes God sustaining every body, including healthy ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Abba, a name for רב (his name was אבא אריכא)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבא' here is not 'father'. It is רב's personal name.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Abba (Rav) has rendered
the whole world sick.
Rather: Healer of all flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: קָא שַׁוִּינְהוּ אַבָּא לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קְצִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ending and proposes a replacement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Healthy people are not sick, so the wording wrongly labels everyone who says it as ill.

steps.title: רב ששת: end with Who does wonders
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת suggests 'מפליא לעשות' as the ending.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: 'Who acts wondrously.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a third opinion with a completely different theme: wonder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of healing, רב ששת focuses on how amazing the body's design is. The theme is God's wonders in creation.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Who acts wondrously.

steps.title: רב פפא: say both endings
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that we combine the endings: 'רופא כל בשר ומפליא לעשות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, let us say both of them: 'Healer of all flesh and Who acts wondrously.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the question by combining the endings of שמואל and רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's version had been rejected, which left two good options. Since each expresses a true theme of the ברכה, רב פפא includes both. This is the ending used today.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say both of them

steps.whatToRemember: אשר יצר ends with 'רופא כל בשר ומפליא לעשות', a combination of שמואל and רב ששת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the standard closing of אשר יצר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ נֵמְרִינְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ —
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore, let us say both of them:
Healer of all flesh and Who acts wondrously.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ נֵמְרִינְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ending of אשר יצר is 'רופא כל בשר ומפליא לעשות'.

steps.title: What to say when going to sleep
steps.stepSummary: Before sleep, one says the first פרשה of קריאת שמע and then the ברכה of המפיל, with its requests for a peaceful, protected night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever goes to sleep in his bed says שמע from 'שמע ישראל' until 'והיה אם שמוע'. Then he says: 'Blessed... Who makes the bands of sleep fall on my eyes and slumber on my eyelids, and Who gives light to the pupil of the eye. May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that You let me lie down in peace and give me my share in Your תורה. Get me used to doing מצוות and do not get me used to sin. Do not bring me to error, wrongdoing, temptation, or disgrace. May the יצר טוב rule over me and not the יצר הרע. Save me from harmful mishaps and bad illnesses. Let bad dreams and bad thoughts not frighten me. May my bed be perfect before You, and light up my eyes so I do not sleep the sleep of death. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who lights up the whole world with His glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the daily routine: what to say at bedtime. It gives the bedtime שמע and the full text of המפיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first paragraph of שמע (until והיה אם שמוע) is required at bedtime. The ברכה then asks for protection through the night: a peaceful sleep, spiritual safety, and no bad dreams. 'מטתי שלמה' means that one's children should be without flaw. It ends with a request to wake up in the morning and not 'sleep the sleep of death'.

keyTerms.meaning: Who makes the bands of sleep fall
My bed is complete (my children are without flaw)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for קריאת שמע על המטה and the ברכת המפיל.

phrases.english: One who goes to sleep on his bed

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר מִ״שְּׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״ עַד ״וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמוֹעַ״,
phrases.english: says from 'Shema Yisrael' until 'VeHaya Im Shamoa',
phrases.notes: That is, the first paragraph of שמע.

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ … הַמַּפִּיל חַבְלֵי שֵׁינָה עַל עֵינַי
phrases.english: and says: Blessed... Who makes the bands of sleep fall upon my eyes
and slumber upon my eyelids,
and gives light to the pupil of the eye.
May it be Your will, ה׳ my God,
that You lay me down in peace,
and give me my portion in Your Torah,
and accustom me to מצוות,
and do not accustom me to transgression,
and do not bring me to error,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לִידֵי עָוֹן, וְלֹא לִידֵי נִסָּיוֹן,
phrases.english: nor to iniquity, nor to temptation,
nor to disgrace.
May the good inclination rule over me,
and may the evil inclination not rule over me.
Save me from harmful mishaps and from bad illnesses.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יְבַהֲלוּנִי חֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים.
phrases.english: Let bad dreams and bad thoughts not frighten me.
May my bed be perfect before You.
phrases.notes: May my children be without flaw.

phrases.english: Light up my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הַמֵּאִיר לָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בִּכְבוֹדוֹ״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who lights up the entire world with His glory.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: At bedtime, one recites the first פרשה of שמע and then the ברכה of המפיל.

steps.title: What to say upon waking up
steps.stepSummary: On waking, one says אלהי נשמה, thanking God for returning the soul.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he wakes up, he says: 'My God, the soul You placed in me is pure. You created it in me, You breathed it into me, You guard it inside me, and one day You will take it from me and return it to me in the time to come. As long as the soul is inside me, I thank You, ה׳ my God and God of my fathers, Master of all worlds, Lord of all souls. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who returns souls to dead bodies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the morning ברכה said on waking: אלהי נשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the bedtime ברכה. At night we ask not to 'sleep the sleep of death', and in the morning we thank God for giving the soul back. The closing, 'returns souls to dead bodies', also points to תחיית המתים in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: In the time to come (תחיית המתים)

steps.whatToRemember: The bedtime and waking ברכות form a pair: המפיל asks to wake up again, and אלהי נשמה thanks God for returning the soul.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the ברכת אלהי נשמה said every morning.

phrases.english: When he wakes up, he says:
My God, the soul You placed in me is pure.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה יְצַרְתָּהּ בִּי, אַתָּה נְפַחְתָּהּ בִּי,
phrases.english: You formed it in me, You breathed it into me,
and You guard it within me,
and You will one day take it from me
and return it to me in the time to come.
As long as the soul is within me

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי,
phrases.english: I give thanks before You, ה׳ my God and God of my fathers,

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹן כׇּל הָעוֹלָמִים, אֲדוֹן כׇּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת.
phrases.english: Master of all worlds, Lord of all souls.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳, הַמַּחֲזִיר נְשָׁמוֹת לִפְגָרִים מֵתִים״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who restores souls to lifeless bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the daily routine from bedtime to waking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upon waking, one recites אלהי נשמה, ending 'המחזיר נשמות לפגרים מתים'.

steps.title: A blessing for each waking action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists a ברכה for each step of getting up: hearing the rooster, opening the eyes, sitting up, dressing, standing straight, stepping down, walking, putting on shoes, belt and head covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he hears the rooster, he should say: Blessed… Who gave the rooster understanding to tell day from night. When he opens his eyes: Blessed… Who opens the eyes of the blind. When he sits up: Blessed… Who frees the bound. When he dresses: Blessed… Who clothes the naked. When he stands up straight: Blessed… Who straightens the bent. When he steps down to the ground: Blessed… Who spreads the earth over the waters. When he walks: Blessed… Who prepares a person's steps. When he puts on his shoes: Blessed… Who has provided me with everything I need. When he ties his belt: Blessed… Who girds Israel with strength. When he spreads a cloth over his head: Blessed… Who crowns Israel with glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the morning routine from step 10 and gives a short ברכה for each small action of waking up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ברכה matches its action. Opening the eyes is like a blind person seeing, sitting up is like a prisoner being freed, and standing straight is like a bent person being raised. The idea is to thank God for every basic ability we usually take for granted.

keyTerms.meaning: rooster (also read by some as 'heart'); the one given understanding to tell day from night
Who opens the eyes of the blind
Who frees those who are bound
Who straightens those who are bent

steps.confusionAlert: שכוי is translated here as 'rooster' because the ברכה comes right when one hears the rooster crow. Sefaria translates it as 'heart'. Both readings exist, but in this context the ברכה is triggered by the rooster.

phrases.english: When he hears the sound of the rooster, he should say:
"Blessed… Who gave the rooster understanding
to tell apart day and night."

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פָּתַח עֵינֵיהּ, לֵימָא: ״בָּרוּךְ … פּוֹקֵחַ עִוְּרִים״.
phrases.english: When he opens his eyes, he should say: "Blessed… Who opens the eyes of the blind."

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תָּרֵיץ וְיָתֵיב, לֵימָא: ״בָּרוּךְ … מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים״.
phrases.english: When he straightens up and sits, he should say: "Blessed… Who frees the bound."
When he dresses, he should say: "Blessed… Who clothes the naked."
When he stands up straight, he should say: "Blessed… Who straightens the bent."
When he steps down to the ground, he should say:
"Blessed… Who spreads the earth over the waters."

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מְסַגֵּי, לֵימָא: ״בָּרוּךְ … הַמֵּכִין מִצְעֲדֵי גָבֶר״.
phrases.english: When he walks, he should say: "Blessed… Who prepares the steps of man."
When he puts on his shoes, he should say:
"Blessed… Who has provided me with all my needs."
When he ties his belt, he should say:
"Blessed… Who girds Israel with strength."

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פָּרֵיס סוּדָרָא עַל רֵישֵׁיהּ, לֵימָא:
phrases.english: When he spreads a cloth on his head, he should say:
"Blessed… Who crowns Israel with glory."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the waking-up sequence that began with אלהי נשמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each waking action is matched by its own ברכה of thanks.

steps.title: מצוה blessings for ציצית, תפילין and נטילת ידים
steps.stepSummary: Next come ברכות on מצוות: wrapping in ציצית, putting תפילין on the arm, putting תפילין on the head, and washing the hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he wraps himself in ציצית, he should say: Blessed… Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to wrap ourselves in ציצית. When he puts תפילין on his arm, he should say: …and commanded us to put on תפילין. On his head, he should say: …and commanded us about the מצוה of תפילין. When he washes his hands, he should say: …and commanded us about washing the hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves from thanking God for natural abilities to ברכות said before doing מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These ברכות use the standard מצוה formula, אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו. תפילין get two different wordings: לְהַנִּיחַ for the arm and עַל מִצְוַת for the head.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us (the standard מצוה-ברכה formula)

phrases.english: When he wraps himself in tzitzis, he should say:
"Blessed… Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to wrap ourselves in tzitzis."
When he puts tefillin on his arm, he should say:
"Blessed… Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to put on tefillin."
On his head, he should say:
"Blessed… Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us regarding the מצוה of tefillin."
When he washes his hands, he should say:
"Blessed… Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us regarding washing the hands."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the morning list, now with מצוה-ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית, arm-תפילין, head-תפילין and נטילת ידים each get a מצוה-ברכה with its own wording.

steps.title: Washing the face: removing sleep, plus a prayer for a good day
steps.stepSummary: When washing the face, one says המעביר שינה, followed by a long יהי רצון asking for help in תורה and מצוות and protection from sin and bad influences. It ends with גומל חסדים טובים לעמו ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he washes his face, he should say: Blessed… Who removes the bands of sleep from my eyes and slumber from my eyelids. May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that You make me used to Your תורה and attach me to Your מצוות. Do not bring me to sin, wrongdoing, a test, or shame. Force my יצר to serve You. Keep me far from a bad person and a bad friend. Attach me to the good יצר and a good friend in Your world. Grant me, today and every day, grace, kindness and mercy in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me, and give me good kindnesses. Blessed are You ה׳, Who gives good kindnesses to His people Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last and longest of the morning ברכות. It thanks God for clearing away sleep, then asks for spiritual protection for the day ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה opens by thanking God for being fully awake. It then turns into a request for a good spiritual day: closeness to תורה, protection from sin and bad company, and favor in others' eyes. The closing line, גומל חסדים טובים, sums up the request for kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: Who removes the bands of sleep
may it be Your will (opening of a request)

steps.whatToRemember: The morning ברכות follow the order of waking up: senses, body, clothing, מצוות, and finally a full prayer for a good spiritual day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the source for the ברכות השחר printed at the start of every סידור.

phrases.english: When he washes his face, he should say:
Blessed… Who removes the bands of sleep from my eyes
and slumber from my eyelids.
And may it be Your will, ה׳ my God,
that You accustom me to Your Torah, and attach me to Your מצוות,
and do not bring me into sin,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לִידֵי עָוֹן, וְלֹא לִידֵי נִסָּיוֹן,
phrases.english: nor into wrongdoing, nor into a test,
nor into disgrace.
Force my inclination to be subservient to You.
Keep me far from a bad person and from a bad friend.

phrases.aramaic: וְדַבְּקֵנִי בְּיֵצֶר טוֹב וּבְחָבֵר טוֹב בְּעוֹלָמֶךָ.
phrases.english: Attach me to the good inclination and to a good friend in Your world.
Grant me, today and every day,
grace, kindness, and mercy
in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me,
and bestow good kindnesses upon me.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who bestows good kindnesses on His people Israel."

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On washing the face one says המעביר שינה with יהי רצון, ending גומל חסדים טובים לעמו ישראל.

steps.title: What does 'bless for the bad as for the good' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line that a person must bless God for bad things just as for good things, and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A person is obligated to bless…' What does 'one must bless over the bad just as one blesses over the good' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks what it means. This sets up the next move, where it will test a possible reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'just as' is unclear. It could mean the same words of ברכה, or the same attitude. The גמרא wants to pin down which one.

keyTerms.meaning: a person is obligated to bless

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] A person is obligated to bless, etc.:
What does "one is obligated to bless over the bad
just as one blesses over the good" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חַיָּיב לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ עַל הַטּוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns to analyze a line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'just as' in the משנה's rule about blessing over bad.

steps.title: It can't mean saying the same blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests it means saying הטוב והמטיב over bad news too. It rejects this, because the משנה itself says that for bad news one says דיין האמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that just as one says 'Who is good and does good' over good things, one also says 'Who is good and does good' over bad things, that is difficult. Didn't we learn in the משנה that over good news one says 'Who is good and does good,' but over bad news one says 'Blessed… the true Judge'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible reading, that the same ברכה is said for bad and good, and shows it contradicts the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly gives two different ברכות: הטוב והמטיב for good news and דיין האמת for bad news. So 'just as' cannot mean the same wording. A different meaning is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: if you will say (introduces a reading about to be rejected)
Who is good and does good
but didn't we learn in a משנה?

steps.confusionAlert: Blessing God for the bad does NOT mean saying הטוב והמטיב over a tragedy. The משנה requires דיין האמת for bad news.

phrases.english: If you say: just as one blesses over the good
"Who is good and does good,"
so one blesses over the bad "Who is good and does good" —
but didn't we learn: over good tidings
one says "Who is good and does good,"
over bad tidings one says
"Blessed… the true Judge"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one possible answer to the question in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the same ברכה (הטוב והמטיב) is said over bad things.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly assigns different ברכות to good and bad news, so the wording cannot be the same.

steps.title: רבא: accept the bad with joy
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה is not about the words of the ברכה. It means one should accept bad news with the same joy as good news.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The line was needed only to teach that one should accept the bad things with joy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the correct meaning of 'just as': it refers to the same attitude, not the same ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכות stay different (דיין האמת versus הטוב והמטיב). What must be the same is the heart: a person says דיין האמת with the same full acceptance and joy as he says הטוב והמטיב.
steps.whatToRemember: Blessing over bad 'as over good' means the same joyful acceptance, not the same words.

phrases.english: Rava said: It was needed only
to [teach us to] accept them with joy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה, אֶלָּא לְקַבּוֹלִינְהוּ בְּשִׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Just as' means the same ברכה wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Just as' means the same joyful acceptance; the ברכות themselves differ.

steps.title: A verse: I sing for kindness and for judgment
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא in the name of רבי לוי brings the פסוק 'חסד ומשפט אשירה' as the source. Whether God gives kindness or strict judgment, I will sing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said in the name of רבי לוי: What is the source verse? 'Of kindness and judgment I will sing; to You, ה׳, I will make music.' If it is kindness, I will sing, and if it is judgment, I will sing.
steps.whatsHappening: A פסוק is brought to support רבא's idea of accepting bad things with joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts חסד (good things) and משפט (hard judgments) side by side, with the same response for both: אשירה, I will sing. This matches the idea that one praises God with joy for the bad as well as the good.
steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק becomes the classic source for the Jewish attitude of accepting hardship with faith and praise.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha said in the name of Rabbi Levi:
What is the verse [for this]?
"Of kindness and judgment I will sing;
to You, ה׳, I will make music."
If it is kindness — I will sing,
and if it is judgment — I will sing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי לֵוִי: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides scriptural support for רבא's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: The duty to accept bad things with joy, like good things.

steps.title: A second source: praising both of God's names
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני brings a פסוק that praises God's word twice, once with the name ה׳ (kindness) and once with אלהים (strict judgment).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: the source is from here: 'With ה׳ I will praise His word; with אלהים I will praise His word.' 'With ה׳ I will praise His word' means God's kind way of acting. 'With אלהים I will praise His word' means God's way of bringing suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source for the idea that we must accept bad things with joy, just as we accept good things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two different names of God. The name ה׳ stands for kindness, and the name אלהים stands for strict judgment and suffering. Since the person says 'I will praise' with both names, he praises God in good times and in hard times alike.
steps.confusionAlert: Sefaria's English flips the order of the names, but our text reads ה׳ first and אלהים second. Either way the point is the same: ה׳ = kindness, אלהים = strict judgment.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: from here:
"With the Lord I will praise His word,
phrases.notes: The name ה׳ stands for kindness

phrases.english: with God I will praise His word" (Psalms 56:11).
phrases.notes: The name אלהים stands for strict judgment

phrases.aramaic: בַּה׳ אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר — זוֹ מִדָּה טוֹבָה,
phrases.english: "With the Lord I will praise His word": this is the attribute of kindness,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּאלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר — זוֹ מִדַּת פּוּרְעָנוּת.
phrases.english: "With God I will praise His word": this is the attribute of suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק as the source for the same idea רבי לוי proved in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that one must accept bad news with joy, just like good news.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Psalms 56:11, which praises God under both the name of kindness (ה׳) and the name of judgment (אלהים).

steps.title: A third source: calling on God in salvation and in trouble
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום brings two פסוקים from Psalms 116 where the same response, 'I will call on the name of ה׳', appears both in times of salvation and in times of trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said: the source is from here: 'I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of ה׳', and 'I find trouble and sorrow, and I call on the name of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a good time (the 'cup of salvation') and in a bad time ('trouble and sorrow') the person does the exact same thing: he calls on the name of ה׳. His reaction to God stays the same no matter what happens. That is what it means to bless God for the bad as for the good.

keyTerms.meaning: Cup of salvation (a time of rescue and joy)
And I will call on the name of ה׳

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum said: from here:
"I will lift up the cup of salvation
and call upon the name of the Lord" (Psalms 116:13),
and: "I find trouble and sorrow,
and I call upon the name of the Lord" (Psalms 116:3–4).
phrases.notes: Same words as phrase 3, showing the same reaction in a bad time

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another different פסוק offered as the source for the same idea.
steps.raayaObject: Accepting bad news with the same joy as good news.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Psalms 116, where the identical response 'ובשם ה׳ אקרא' follows both salvation and trouble.

steps.title: A fourth source: איוב blesses God after loss
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן bring איוב's famous words after losing everything: 'ה׳ gave and ה׳ took; may the name of ה׳ be blessed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: the source is from here: 'ה׳ has given and ה׳ has taken; may the name of ה׳ be blessed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth source, this time from איוב, for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב sees both the giving and the taking as coming from the same God. Right after his terrible losses he blesses God's name. This is a clear real-life example of blessing God for the bad just as for the good.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the general group of rabbis)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: from here:
"The Lord has given and the Lord has taken away;
blessed be the name of the Lord" (Job 1:21).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of the list of alternative sources for the same idea.
steps.raayaObject: Accepting bad news with the same joy as good news.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Job 1:21, where איוב blesses God right after his great losses.

steps.title: Always say: everything God does is for the best
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב, quoting רבי מאיר (and a ברייתא quoting רבי עקיבא), teaches that a person should get used to saying 'Everything the Merciful One does, He does for the best.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב, quoting רבי מאיר, and the same was taught in the name of רבי עקיבא: A person should always be used to saying, 'Everything the Merciful One does, He does for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the list of sources, the גמרא gives a practical habit that puts this idea into daily life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources showed that we must praise God even for the bad. This teaching goes one step further: train yourself to say out loud that whatever God does is for the good. The word רגיל ('used to') means this should be a constant habit, not something said only once in a while.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Used to, in the habit of

steps.whatToRemember: Bad news gets a different ברכה (דיין האמת) but the same joyful acceptance. Many פסוקים teach this, and the habit to build is saying: כל דעביד רחמנא לטב עביד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This short line became one of the most famous Jewish attitudes toward hardship. It is the practical goal of the whole discussion of the משנה's rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said in the name of Rabbi Meir,
and so it was taught in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
A person should always be accustomed to saying:
"Everything that the Merciful One does, He does for the good."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְכֵן תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from finding sources for the idea to giving a practical daily habit based on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always train himself to say: everything God does is for the good.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is turned away from the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story to illustrate the teaching. רבי עקיבא is refused lodging in a city, and he responds, 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the best.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the story of רבי עקיבא, who was traveling on the road. He came to a certain city and asked for a place to stay, but they would not give him one. He said: 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the best.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a story to show the teaching from the last step in real life. The first bad thing happens: רבי עקיבא has nowhere to sleep, and he still says 'it is for the best.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כי הא ('like this') tell us the story is an example of the rule just taught in רבי עקיבא's name. The first setback is a real inconvenience, since he must now sleep outside. His reaction shows the habit the teaching asks for: he says the phrase right away, before he knows of any good outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Lodging, a place to stay as a guest

phrases.english: Like this incident of Rabbi Akiva
phrases.notes: Links the story to the teaching in step 21.

phrases.english: who was traveling on the road.
He came to a certain city,
he asked for lodging, but they did not give him any.
He said: 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the good.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דַּהֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that shows the teaching of step 21 in action.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching that a person should always say 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the best.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רבי עקיבא himself, the one quoted in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא loses his candle, rooster, and donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא sleeps in a field. Wind puts out his candle, a cat eats his rooster, and a lion eats his donkey. He again says, 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the best.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and slept in a field. He had with him a rooster, a donkey, and a candle. A wind came and blew out the candle. A cat came and ate the rooster. A lion came and ate the donkey. He said: 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the best.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues, and things get worse. רבי עקיבא loses everything he has with him, one item after another, and he says the same phrase again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These losses are worse than the first one: no light, no rooster to wake him, and no donkey to carry him. רבי עקיבא's answer does not change, which shows the phrase is a fixed habit and not a one-time comment. The three items will matter later in the story, so the learner should remember them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rooster (used to wake people at dawn)

phrases.english: He went and slept in the field,
and he had with him a rooster, a donkey, and a candle.
phrases.notes: Keep these three items in mind. They become important at the end.

phrases.english: A wind came and blew out the candle.
A cat came and ate the rooster.
A lion came and ate the donkey.
He said: 'Everything the Merciful One does is for the good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with even bigger losses, met with the same response.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching to say 'it is for the best' even when things keep getting worse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuing story of רבי עקיבא's night in the field.

steps.title: An army captures the city, and רבי עקיבא explains
steps.stepSummary: That same night, an army captures the city. רבי עקיבא says to them, 'Didn't I tell you, everything that הקדוש ברוך הוא does…' The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: That very night, an army came and took the city captive. He said to them: 'Didn't I tell you? Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does…'
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its turning point. The city that turned him away is captured, and רבי עקיבא starts to explain that his losses were for the good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had he stayed in the city, he would have been captured too. Had his candle been lit, his rooster crowing, or his donkey braying, the soldiers could have found him in the field. Every loss turned out to protect him. This proves the teaching from step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of רבי עקיבא's sentence. The final words, 'הכל לטובה' ('is all for the good'), come on the next amud. Also, the גמרא never says outright that the candle, rooster, and donkey would have given him away. That explanation, found in the Sefaria brackets, is how we understand the story, not words in the text itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows that the habit of saying 'it is for the best' is not denial. It reflects trust that God's plan, which we may not see yet, is good.

phrases.english: That very night an army came,
and took the city captive.
He said to them: Didn't I tell you,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does…
phrases.notes: Here he speaks in Hebrew, not Aramaic. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the outcome that makes sense of all the earlier losses.
steps.raayaObject: That 'everything the Merciful One does is for the best' is really true, not just a pious saying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The army's capture of the city, which רבי עקיבא escaped only because of his losses.
